hook: Put a pot of water on the stove. The temperature climbs steadily to 100 °C, then stops, even though the burner is still on full. For several minutes the water just boils, sitting at 100 °C. All that energy is going somewhere, but not into making the water hotter.

prereq.q: When water boils, what is overcome?
options: O–H covalent bonds inside each molecule
prereq.why: Phase changes overcome attractions between molecules; the molecules stay intact.

prereq.q: How much energy warms 10.0 g of water by 5.0 °C? (c = 4.18 J/(g·°C))

figure.caption: On the sloped parts one phase warms (q = mcΔT). On the flat parts two phases coexist and the temperature stays constant (q = nΔH).

chain.cause: Energy is added to a solid
chain.effect: its particles vibrate faster and its temperature rises until it reaches the melting point

chain.cause: At the melting point, added energy overcomes the attractions holding particles in place
chain.effect: the solid melts at constant temperature; potential energy rises, kinetic energy does not

chain.cause: Once melted, added energy speeds the particles up again
chain.effect: the liquid warms until the boiling point

chain.cause: Boiling separates the particles almost completely
chain.effect: the boiling plateau is longest: ΔHvap is larger than ΔHfus
condensing and freezing release the same energies: q = −nΔH

ideas: The enthalpy of fusion (ΔHfus) is the energy to melt 1 mol of solid at its melting point; the enthalpy of vaporization (ΔHvap) is the energy to vaporize 1 mol of liquid.
Melting, vaporizing and subliming absorb energy (q = +nΔH); freezing and condensing release it (q = −nΔH).
ΔHvap > ΔHfus: vaporizing separates molecules almost completely.
On a heating curve, slopes use q = mcΔT and flat parts use q = nΔH; add the steps.
Stronger attractions between particles mean larger ΔHfus and ΔHvap.

misconception.wrong: While water boils, the energy from the burner makes the water molecules move faster.
misconception.right: The temperature stays at 100 °C, so the average speed of the molecules does not change. The energy goes into separating the molecules from each other.

summary: During a phase change, energy overcomes (or forms) attractions between particles, so the temperature stays constant. The energy is n × ΔHfus for melting and n × ΔHvap for boiling, with ΔHvap the larger. A heating curve combines sloped parts (q = mcΔT) and flat parts (q = nΔH).
